item.title: Golfers Gain Distance By Fixing Attack Angle Numbers
item.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images Most avid golfers track their swing speed, yet many ignore the single metric that changes distance the most. Attack angle determines whether the club moves up or down at the moment of impact. This number dictates launch height and spin rates more than almost any other factor in the game. According to MyGolfSpy , a positive angle means the club moves upward, while a negative angle indicates a downward strike. The ideal number differs completely between the driver and irons, a fact that often confuses players who try to hit every club the same way. Understanding this distinction allows a golfer to maximize carry distance without increasing swing speed. MyGolfSpy reports that inconsistent attack angles can cause high-handicap players to see over 30 yards of carry variation. The same golfer with the same speed can hit shots 12 yards apart just by changing the angle of attack. This gap exists because the club path interacts with the ball differently depending on whether it is teed up or sitting on the turf. The Driver Requires an Upward Strike With the driver, the goal is to hit the ball on an upward strike. Golfers should tee the ball high and position it toward the front of the stance to facilitate this motion. MyGolfSpy explains that hitting up helps in two specific ways: it launches the ball higher and reduces spin. High launch combined with low spin creates the optimal conditions for maximum distance. Data provided by GOLFJOY and cited by MyGolfSpy shows a clear difference when comparing a -5 degree angle to a +5 degree angle. When a golfer swings at 80 mph, hitting down on the ball produces a lower trajectory with excessive spin that kills distance. Conversely, hitting up with a +5 degree angle optimizes the launch conditions. Reports note that the same swing speed yields vastly different results based solely on this vertical club path. Players who try to hit down on the driver are fighting the physics of the club design. Irons Demand a Slight Downward Angle Irons work in the opposite direction compared to the driver. The ball sits on the ground, so the club must strike the ball first and then the turf. This sequence ensures clean contact and proper spin to hold the green. MyGolfSpy states that the sweet spot for a 7-iron is roughly 2 to 5 degrees downward. Striking the ball with too little or too much downward angle costs significant distance. An 80 mph swing with a -4 degree angle produces a launch of 18 degrees, which represents the middle option that wins for most players. Deviating from this range leads to poor contact. If the angle is too flat, the club may catch the turf before the ball. If the angle is too steep, the player might thin the shot or lose energy transfer. The data shows that the middle option within the 2 to 5 degree range consistently delivers the best results for carry and control. item.title: Mets’ Johnny Washington Hire Leaves Braves Fans With Big Questions
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The New York Mets just made a move that stings for Atlanta fans. They hired Johnny Washington as a co-hitting coach, pulling him right from the Braves’ organization. Washington served as the Braves’ minor league hitting coordinator during the 2026 season. The Mets are now stacking three hitting coaches in one room, a setup that feels strange for a team that needs immediate offense. A Familiar Name in a New Spot Washington is not a stranger to the Mets. Andy Green, the current Mets manager, previously employed him with the San Diego Padres and subsequently the Chicago Cubs. The hiring was reported by Joel Sherman of the New York Post, who noted the Mets finally have a new coach after weeks of searching. They fired their previous hitting coordinator, Jeff Albert, after just one season in the role. Washington joins Troy Snitker and Rafael Fernandez. The situation looks odd because the Mets missed out on top targets. Prior to selecting Washington, they consulted John Mallee of the Chicago Cubs and Kevin Long of the Philadelphia Phillies. Each was considered a top contender to direct the staff. Instead, the Mets turned to a familiar voice from Green’s past. This choice suggests they could not land the big names they wanted. The Braves, meanwhile, kept Tim Hyers as their hitting coach despite a lackluster offensive season. Why the Braves Let Him Go Braves fans have to ask why Washington slipped through their fingers. The team kept Hyers even though the offense ranked eighth in runs but had the third-fewest walks in MLB. Their on-base percentage of .309 was a full point lower than the Mets. In 2026, only the Colorado Rockies and San Francisco Giants posted a lower on-base rate than Atlanta. Washington would have signaled a change, but the Braves chose stability over a new voice. Washington’s past has its own baggage, though. He was the hitting coach for the Los Angeles Angels when they posted poor numbers. In 2024, the Angels batted .226 with him. Year two saw them hit .225. Before his Angels departure, a Reddit discussion noted an interview regarding his hitting philosophy. Critics labeled him a home run enthusiast who promoted a “wait for your pitch and end the at-bat” philosophy, according to Rising Apple . The Mets hired a coach with a mixed track record. The Mets cannot afford to repeat their offensive struggles from last season. They ranked in the bottom 10 in on-base percentage, slugging percentage, and runs scored. With Francisco Lindor and Juan Soto back healthy, the offense must improve. The Brewers had four hitting coaches last season and won the World Series. Milwaukee utilized a lead coach, whereas the Mets allegedly lack such a role currently.

item.title: Jessica Pegula jokes about 'hot mic' incident at WTA Finals media day
item.description: American tennis star Jessica Pegula wasted little time defusing the tension around the well-documented "hot mic" incident during her appearance with media Friday ahead of the WTA Finals. As Pegula entered the room and sat down at the front of the press conference, she grabbed the microphone and playfully tapped it and said "OK, the mic's on. Just wanted to be sure." Her joke drew a laugh from the assembled media. Pegula was referencing an incident that happened earlier in the week when a microphone on the practice court that was intended to just pick up ambient noise of tennis balls hitting the hardcourt and environmental sounds for a livestream, actually picked up a conversation between Pegula and one of her coaches during a practice session. On the live stream she was heard calling another tour player Mirra Andreeva a "diva" among other comments in what she thought was a private discussion. A spokesperson for Pegula has since reported that Pegula "had absolutely no idea that her conversation with (her coach) was being livestreamed and certainly never expected a private discussion during practice to be made public." Pegula has since apologized to the other players involved. For its part, the WTA has taken full responsibility and apologized to Pegula for the incident. On Friday, WTA Chair Valerie Camillo, who spoke to the media minutes before Pegula did, struck a different tone that Pegula's light-hearted opener. She was quite serious. She said livestreaming practices is an attempt to bring fans closer to the game and they have done it before, using the similar ambient noise effect, but in this case mistakes were made. "There were several breakdowns in our execution of the livestream, given our own policies and procedures. There was a lack of advanced notice and clear signage to assist players about the recording equipment operating in the area and it was also not our intention to capture conversations on the livestream of practices but rather to record ambient sound. So clearly there was a failure in our technical execution. As the chair of the WTA I'm committed to leading an organization that delivers the best for our players, our tournaments and our fans. Our execution here did not meet that standard," she said. "I want to specifically apologize to Jessica Pegula, what happened was regrettable and unacceptable. Jess is one of the WTA's best advocates and biggest start and she does not deserve this distraction. One of the primary responsibilities of the WTA is to protect our players whenever possible. ANd that did not happen here. Players deserve better and we will continue to work to raise the bar at the WTA." Camillo went on to say that the sound has been disabled now on the practice courts for the rest of this event. item.title: Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles' injury shakes up clash against Iowa
item.description: The big Iowa -Northwestern matchup got a Friday surprise, one day before the Nov. 7 kickoff at Ryan Field (6:30 p.m., FOX). ESPN’s Pete Thamel reported that star Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles, who had been listed as questionable on the first two injury reports of the week, will miss the game against the Hawkeyes with an upper-body injury. Nicco Marchiol, a left-handed transfer from West Virginia who has attempted one pass this season, is expected to make the start against an Iowa defense that ranks No. 4 nationally. Veteran back-up Nicco Marchiol will make the start for Northwestern, his first start for the Wildcats. He’s a veteran who has a 6-2 record as a starter while at West Virginia. He’s played in 27 career games. — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) November 6, 2026 The sudden move shifted the betting line. Iowa went from a 2½-point underdog to a 2½-point favorite as of early Friday afternoon. The 19th-ranked Hawkeyes (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten Conference) spoke earlier this week about wanting to atone for a poor 2024 performance against Chiles when he was with Michigan State and dominated Iowa, 32-20, in East Lansing. Chiles had been playing fantastic football, having thrown 13 touchdowns and rushed for 10 more with just one interception through eight games this fall. He has been the catalyst for Chip Kelly’s unique offense that catered to his dual-threat capabilities. And while it is seemingly a benefit for Iowa to face Northwestern (6-2, 3-2) without its star quarterback, it does throw a lot of preparations made all week into the trash can. While Northwestern probably won’t change its style of offense, Marchiol does bring a less-mobile presence to the field. But he does have experience. Marchiol started seven games during his four seasons at West Virginia, including the first four of 2025 before suffering a season-ending foot injury. He completed 66 of 98 passes (67.3%) for 720 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions last season while posting a 3-1 record for the Mountaineers. Iowa is coming off a 30-0 home shutout of then-No. 25 Wisconsin at Kinnick Stadium and needs to win its final four regular-season games to have a shot at the College Football Playoff. This bit of quarterback news would seem to help the cause, at least a little bit. Hawkeyes columnist Chad Leistikow has served for 32 years with The Des Moines Register and USA TODAY Sports Network. item.title: Janja Garnbret conquered Bibliographie. Her next climb: unprecedented Olympic heights
item.description: Janja Garnbret made history on June 6 by becoming the first woman to climb Bibliographie, a 115-foot route on a limestone cliff in Céüse, France. Her sights are now set on another unprecedented feat — capturing two Olympic gold medals in climbing at one Games in Los Angeles in 2028. Garnbret, a 27-year-old from Slovenia, already won the combined at the Tokyo Games and the Paris Games, the first two Olympics to include her sport. "After both Olympics, I felt I like to call it a black period or something," she said. "I felt really unmotivated. I asked myself if I will ever be able to top again anything. Everybody prepares you for the competition, but no one really prepares you for what comes after. … I just needed to wait for the motivation to come back." Climbing had one competition in Tokyo — an event combining the disciplines of speed, boulder and lead. For Paris, it was split into two events — a combined event for boulder and lead plus an event for speed only. In LA, each of the three disciplines will have its own set of medals. "I think this is what we all wanted right from the beginning," Garnbret said. Garnbret began climbing whatever she could grasp by age 7 — trees, closets and doors. She has competed internationally in boulder and lead since age 14. She trained speed for the Tokyo Games, then dropped it from her repertoire afterward once it was no longer part of the Olympic combined event. In LA, the women's boulder and lead semifinals are back-to-back days, followed by a day off, and then back-to-back days of the finals. Garnbret has no preference between boulder and lead, having won the most recent world title in each in 2025. But this year, her focus was on Bibliographie. She recently toured the U.S. , promoting a film documenting her ascent. She said that only five people previously scaled it — all men. She trekked to it for the first time two weeks after the Paris Olympics. It took 21 sessions spread across the next two years to complete it. "I fell asleep thinking about the route," she said. "I woke up thinking about the route." Yet she still competed off and on in the Olympic disciplines on the World Series circuit in 2026. item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images LIV Golf is officially finished. The league announced on Thursday that it will not restructure and is moving toward full liquidation after losing its financier, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund. This ends a period of division that split professional golf into competing tours. The answer depends on specific contractual obligations and the Tour’s stance on meritocracy. Brian Rolapp, the PGA Tour CEO, has made it clear that the path back is not automatic for anyone who defected. LIV officials announced they are ending the league this week, leaving players such as Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau with uncertain futures for the 2027 season. Rory McIlroy, the league’s most outspoken critic, took one last jab before the collapse. “They turned professional golf into an arms race,” McIlroy declared earlier this week, according to Yahoo Sports . The league’s demise leaves these stars without a tour, forcing them to consider other options. The DP World Tour remains a destination for some, as the current top 10 in the Race to Dubai secure PGA Tour cards. item.title: Has the Detroit Lions defense turned a corner?
item.description: What a difference a month can make. After a historically bad start to the season, Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has helped the defense find their sea legs over the course of the last four weeks. With that said, there is still plenty to improve upon for a unit that has even more to play for with the loss of All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell during their Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings. There were some around the fan base and media who were ready to move on from Sheppard if things didn’t improve—especially after the loss to the Carolina Panthers where they appeared to be out-schemed from the jump. After some tough conversations as well as some schematic and personnel tweaks, the Lions’ defense is beginning to settle in dating back to their Week 5 whooping of the Arizona Cardinals. That brings us to today’s Question of the Day: Do you believe the Lions’ defense has turned a corner? My answer: Despite a three-game sample size not being the largest to go off of, I do belive this unit has begun to figure things out. It still isn’t perfect, and there are still too many missed assignments for my liking, but you can do a lot with the way the Lions’ front is playing. Their star players up front, like defensive end Aidan Hutchinson and defensive tackle Alim McNeill, are making their presence felt nearly every time the ball is snapped. Beyond those two, other members of the defensive line like rookie Skyler Gill-Howard and second year defensive tackle Tyleik Williams are playing some really good football. And while there are still things to clean up in the secondary, cornerback D.J. Reed’s play has really leveled out, star defensive back Brian Branch is back in the mix, and the team opened up All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph’s 21-day window last week. If they can continue to defend the run well and cut down on the blown coverage moments that have plagued them through seven games, I think that will be enough to make them a contender down the stretch. Continue to improve so that you are playing your best, and most sound football in December and into January. When you have an offense like Detroit does, that’s all you really need. What about you? item.title: John Gibson Returns to Practice With Detroit’s Net Unsettled
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings have a goaltending decision to make before Saturday, and John Gibson practicing again just made it a harder one. Gibson was back on the ice Friday after leaving Tuesday’s game at Tampa Bay with a lower-body injury, Detroit Free Press reporter Helene St. James reported. He is still listed as day to day rather than cleared, so the question in front of Detroit is not only when Gibson is available, but whether he should get the net back when he is. Nov 3, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Detroit Red Wings goaltender John Gibson (36) makes a save during the first period against Tampa Bay Lightning at Benchmark International Arena. Mandatory Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) John Gibson Practiced, but He Is Not Cleared to Play St. James reported that Gibson took part in Friday’s practice, and nothing beyond that. Gibson missed Thursday’s game against the Vegas Golden Knights, and the reporting on his status stops short of Saturday , when the Red Wings open a road trip against the Colorado Avalanche on Nov. 7 . Detroit has not named a starter for that game. John Gibson Is Having a Bad Season for the Detroit Red Wings Gibson has played 11 games for the Red Wings this season. He has a 4-5-1 record with a 3.46 GAA and a .860 save percentage. Gibson has struggled big time and is 33 years old and in the final year of his contract , the eight-year deal he signed in Anaheim that carries a $6.4 million cap hit and sends him to unrestricted free agency this summer. He has not played well at all this season, and even though Gibson is back at practice, it may not be time for him to get the starting net back. Keep Daniil Tarasov and Michal Postava as the Goaltending Tandem Even if Gibson were to be healthy, the Red Wings should make him a healthy scratch. He provides nothing to the team at this point. A goaltending tandem of Daniil Tarasov and Michal Postava makes the Red Wings much more competitive between the pipes. Tarasov started for Detroit against the Vegas Golden Knights in a 2-1 loss on Thursday night , turning aside 32 shots in a game Detroit lost on a goal with 1:42 left . He has played in seven games this season for the Red Wings. Tarasov has a 2-2-2 record with a 1.79 GAA and a .930 save percentage, along with one shutout. item.title: Utah State vs. Fresno State: How to watch, listen to or stream the game
item.description: Utah State quarterback McCae Hillstead (2) runs down the field as Colorado State cornerback CJ Blocker (17) defends Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, in Logan. | Eli Lucero/Herald Journal Utah State (3-5, 2-2) vs. Fresno State (5-3, 3-1) Kickoff: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. MST Venue: Maverik Stadium TV: USA Sports Radio: Aggie Sports Network (KZNS 1280 The Zone) Series: Utah State and Fresno State have played 34 times since their first meeting in 1952. Fresno State leads all-time 19-14. Utah State has lost two of its last three games to the Bulldogs but won last year’s matchup, 28-17. The trends For Utah State: The Aggies are riding high after their performance against Colorado State last week. Utah State’s struggling offense has been the headliner all year, and it had a breakthrough with a season-high 31 points in a convincing 31-14 win. Quarterback McCae Hillstead made his first start since the season opener, and he looked great. Hillstead threw for 173 yards while completing 77% of his passes. He also ran for 79 yards on 11 carries and pulled in a 44-yard reception on a trick play from Anthony Garcia. Most importantly, Hillstead didn’t have any turnovers. The biggest caveat to all of this is that Colorado State is one of the worst defenses in the country. Still, it was the first time all year the offense was consistent on drives and moving the ball. For Fresno State: The Bulldogs are also coming off a confidence-boosting win over Oregon State, especially with how the previous few weeks went. Fresno State was rolling until it hosted Boise State in early October. The Bulldogs battled, but Boise State eked out a 38-31 win. Then the following week, Fresno State gave up 10 in the fourth quarter to San Diego State and lost 26-23. After a bye week, the Bulldogs were back in action and got a big 38-22 win over Oregon State. The Beavers were previously undefeated in Pac-12 play. What to watch for Is this a turning point for the offense? Utah State had its best offensive performance last week, and Hillstead looked the part of a starting quarterback. However, it’s difficult to determine if that result was because of natural offensive growth or because the Aggies played the statistically worst defense in the country. There’s probably truth somewhere in the middle, and Utah State will face a much tougher test against Fresno State. On average, the Bulldogs hold opponents to 21 points per game. That ranks 40th in the country. Meanwhile, Utah State averages just 17 points per game. Saturday will show if the offense has improved, if a healthy Hillstead is what it needed, or if the offense regresses to where it was before the Colorado State win. Protect the football and the quarterback: Utah State played some close games early in the season, and turnovers especially burned it against Idaho State and Washington. However, Hillstead and Grady Brosterhous have now gone three straight games without an interception. The last interception was one Hillstead threw against Boise State.

item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA - JULY 22, 2024: Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Chris Taylor (3) works with Dodgers batting coach Aaron Bates before the game against the San Francisco Giants at Dodgers Stadium on July 22, 2024 in Los Angeles, CA.(Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) For the first time in three years, there will be a change in the Dodgers coaching staff for 2027, as hitting coach Aaron Bates won’t return. Tim Dierkes of MLB Trade Rumors was first to report the coaching change , which was also reported by Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times , Jack Harris of the California Post , and others. “The Dodgers offered Bates a multiyear contract to stay, but the two sides couldn’t agree to terms,” Dierkes wrote . Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman in his season-ending press conference at Dodger Stadium on October 21 was asked if there would be any coaching changes this offseason. “I expect status quo,” Friedman said. “We’re still working through some things, but expect status quo.” Bates, 42, was on the Dodgers major league coaching staff during the last eight seasons, including the last four as hitting coach along with Robert Van Scoyoc . Bates from 2019-22 held a dual role as assistant hitting coach on the major league staff and director of hitting for the minor league system . As a player, Bates was a third-round draft pick of the Boston Red Sox in 2006 out of North Carolina State, and he played in five games in the majors for Boston in 2009. The corner outfielder and first baseman played for nine seasons in the minors, ending with 11 games for Double-A Chattanooga in the Dodgers’ system in 2014. Bates was in the Dodgers organization for 13 years, including 12 years as a coach. item.title: "We failed so we had to react" - Fred Vasseur on Ferrari driver talks and Mexico F1 fallout
item.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari F1 chief Fred Vasseur insists he has cleared the air with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton after their highly publicised Mexican Grand Prix clash last week. At the Mexico City event, Hamilton and Leclerc both went off track on lap one as they fought for the lead, with Hamilton losing a position to Max Verstappen instead, while Leclerc was penalised and eventually also ceded the lead to the Red Bull driver. Verstappen went on to win the race with Hamilton second and Leclerc off the podium in fourth, with the sabre-rattling on lap one robbing the team of a possible third win of the campaign. Hamilton was particularly furious about how Leclerc had raced him at the start, lobbying for the stewards to hand his team-mate a bigger penalty for cutting the track. The seven-time world champion demanded serious talks with Leclerc and Vasseur over how hard his team-mate was racing him, while Vasseur was frustrated with what he felt was a lack of respect towards Maranello's 2,000-strong staff trying to provide both drivers with a winning car. Those talks have since happened on Thursday night in Sao Paulo, and speaking to the media for the first time since last weekend, Vasseur was adamant the message to both of his drivers was loud and clear. Ferrari must always come first. "The guidelines are always the same. They are two competitors with a fighting spirit for sure, but they need to have respect for each other," Vasseur said. "But mainly and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working on track. I think we are putting a lot of effort on this and the message was clear and will stay clear." Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari On Thursday Hamilton said he agreed with suggestions that Leclerc was racing him harder than he raced other drivers, his team boss pointed towards Leclerc's aggressive overtake on Verstappen in Austin to downplay those claims. "He said that he was fighting probably a bit harder with him than with some others, but if you have a look at what Charles did in Austin in the first sector, everybody said that it was magic," Vasseur said. "The line is fine between the two. But he didn't crash into the other car." The Frenchman added: "For sure, in this situation, we failed collectively because we were one and two and we didn't win the race at the end. That means that it's clear that we failed and we have to react. "But the conclusion of the meeting yesterday evening was clear that it was a clear reminder that the Ferrari is coming first, is coming first for the brand, for the employees, for the Tifosi, and this we have to keep it in mind." item.description: Giants coach/football czar John Harbaugh has said he wants a Derrick Henry-type running back — a sure-thing No. 1 guy. So why not pick up the phone and call his old Baltimore buddies, to see if Henry might be available before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline? The Ravens are going nowhere this season without Lamar Jackson. They’re 4-5 after Thursday night’s beatdown at the hands of the Jaguars. Baltimore has now lost four straight games. Henry is an all-time great back in the twilight of his career — but can still be productive. (Or so it seems.) Plus, Henry is quite frustrated. He made that obvious after Thursday night’s game. “I mean, we’ve lost four times [in a row],” Henry said . “It’s frustrating. I don’t have the magical answer. We’ve got to go back to work.” When asked about a potential trade, Henry said, “I have not mentioned me going anywhere else. I’m saying let’s go back to work.” Henry turns 33 in January. He is under contract through next season. Harbaugh doesn’t want a one-year rental, and Henry technically would not be that. His salary next year is $11 million — all of which is non-guaranteed. He has a $1 million roster bonus due in March. So the Ravens (or Giants) have a team option on him for 2027. If the Ravens believe they will move on from Henry (via release) after 2026, they wouldn’t be eligible for a compensatory draft pick tied to his departure. So they might as well get something for now him, right? MORE BY DARRYL SLATER Giants-Eagles injury report: Troubling news on Cam Skattebo, Malik Nabers? He is five years younger than Henry and is under contract through 2028, with salaries of $15 million and $9.4 million, with a $7.5 million (team option) roster bonus in 2028. The outspoken former Premier League boss has targeted United's recent signings, challenging why a club of their standing continues to invest heavily in attacking and midfield personnel while neglecting to build a dependable defense. "They spend money on forwards, they spend money on midfield players like you've never seen and yet they still haven't got a defense," Warnock said while speaking at a shoot for an upcoming Famous Grouse Christmas campaign, via The Mirror . item.description: Heading into the NFL trade deadline next Tuesday, the Buffalo Bills are going to be an interesting team to keep an eye on. Following a 6-1 start, they are looking the part of a top-tier Super Bowl contender. While the Bills have played great football so far this season, there are still some clear needs to address before the deadline. Looking at the roster, Buffalo could use help on the defensive side of the football. Two positions to consider improving would be cornerback and defensive end. NFL insider Vic Carucci has named Washington Commanders safety Nick Cross as a potential fit for Buffalo. Cross is playing in his first year with the Commanders. He played the first four years of his NFL career with the Indianapolis Colts after being selected with the No. 96 overall pick in the third round of the 2022 NFL Draft. item.description: Warriors reportedly want to sign $276M three-time MVP, NBA champion to pair with Steph Curry originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The future of Nikola Jokic in Denver remains uncertain, as he could have the opportunity to choose where he wants to play this summer. His long-term future with the Denver Nuggets is not as clear as it once seemed. In fact, the Nuggets are prepared to offer Jokic the largest contract in NBA history. His projected deal could be worth a staggering $360 million. “Every league source I've spoken to over the years and in recent weeks has reiterated that no one really expects Jokić to leave Denver. Waiting also makes financial sense: Next summer, he could sign a projected five-year, $360 million deal — the richest deal in NBA history," Yahoo Sports’ Kevin O'Connor wrote. Although Jokic could secure that lucrative contract by staying in Denver, other teams are already monitoring his situation and hoping to have a chance to pursue him in free agency. “While the best Nugget ever has insisted that he wants to stay in Denver and sign a massive five-year deal worth a projected $360 million, there is justifiable paranoia in the Mile High City that the shortcomings of the rest of the roster may cause his eye to wander. Certainly, 29 other teams are scheming for how they might lure him away come July," The Athletic’s John Hollinger wrote. One team hoping to land the three-time MVP is the Golden State Warriors . Adding Jokic could give the organization another opportunity to chase a championship with Steph Curry. “The Warriors are one of those teams out there that are looking around and rubbing their fingers together and thinking, ‘Are we sure Jokic isn’t gonna become available next summer?'” NBA insider Jake Fischer reported Thursday on Deals and Dunks. A move like this would give the Warriors an incredibly difficult offense to defend. If they can move Kristaps Porziņģis' contract and allow several expiring contracts to come off the books without re-signing those players, they could have a path toward creating the necessary cap flexibility. Jokic is currently playing under a $276 million contract with the Nuggets. Pairing him with Curry would give Golden State an elite duo capable of making another serious championship push. If the Warriors are serious about pursuing Jokic, they could make a major run at him if he reaches free agency. item.title: 'Unexplained neurological symptoms' behind Henderson absence
item.description: TreVeyon Henderson has played six times for the Patriots this season [Getty Images] TreVeyon Henderson says "a series of unexplained neurological symptoms", which resulted in him being admitted to hospital, are the reason for his absence for the New England Patriots. The 24-year-old running back was listed on his side's injury report on 29 October with an illness and missed the win against the Miami Dolphins last weekend. The Patriots have listed Henderson as not having taken part in practice prior to Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers, a game he is expected to miss. "Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalisation for several days," said Henderson in a statement on social media. "During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable. "I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, co-ordination, and some of my physical functions. "I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health. My health and long-term wellbeing remain my foremost priorities." Henderson has figured six times for the Patriots this season, registering one touchdown and rushing for 203 yards from 52 attempts.
